name: XLZD
summary: XLZD brings together xenon-detector groups to develop a next-generation observatory for dark matter, neutrinos and rare decays. It succeeds the separate DARWIN design effort and draws on XENON and LZ detector experience.
detection_principle: A large dual-phase liquid-xenon time projection chamber provides three-dimensional localization, scintillation and ionization measurements. Solar and supernova neutrinos and xenon-136 double-beta decay form part of the programme.

status.evidence: The design and sensitivity papers study a 60-80-tonne active xenon observatory. Their half-life and neutrino sensitivities are projections for a future instrument.

results.summary: The design and sensitivity papers study a 60-80-tonne active xenon observatory. Their half-life and neutrino sensitivities are projections for a future instrument.

science_scope: A neutrinoless decay would violate lepton number. Half-life sensitivity is a forecast unless explicitly reported as an experimental limit; its interpretation as an effective Majorana mass depends on the decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements.
